content:
iOS 27 is a major update to Apple's Photos app, improving features such as slideshow presentations and Shared Albums. It also adds a long-awaited camera roll-like feature: "Captured by Me".

The "Captured by Me" section in the iOS 27 Photos app will only show photos and videos that you take and record with the Camera app.

Apple's Photos app has been expanding its features over the years. In addition to storing photos and videos taken with your iPhone, it also includes content shared by friends, "Memories", screenshots, saved media, and more.

The Photos app used to have a "Camera Roll" feature, similar to how the "Recents" album works today, which would show photos you took yourself, as well as images you saved.

However, it has always lacked a feature that only shows photos and videos you took yourself—in other words, a more aptly named "Camera Roll".

iOS 27 finally fills this long-missing gap, and it's called "Captured by Me".

The "Captured by Me" in iOS 27 is a brand-new collection category in Photos, and as the name suggests, it only includes media captured with your Camera app.

So the photos and videos you take with your iPhone will be gathered in one place. Screenshots, images sent by friends, or other types of content will not appear.

In addition to having a dedicated "Captured by Me" collection category, you can also use the "Captured by Me" filter in the main Photos library.

Whichever way you use it, the "Captured by Me" feature in iOS 27 fills an important gap in Apple's Photos functionality.

Will you use this new feature in the iOS 27 Photos app? Feel free to let us know in the comments section.
